name: Fosfomycin
executiveSummary: Antibacterial. Uncomplicated adult cystitis: fosfomycin trometamol **3 g PO once**. IV (disodium): adults often 12–24 g/day in divided doses; pediatric IV 200–400 mg/kg/day.
indications:
## Indications

- **Trometamol PO**: acute uncomplicated cystitis in women (and other uses per local label).
- **Disodium IV**: severe infections due to susceptible organisms (including some MDR) when antibiogram and ID indicate.

## Precautions

- Trometamol: metoclopramide, antacids, and Ca salts ↓ absorption.
- IV disodium: high **Na⁺** content (~14.5 mEq per gram) — caution in heart failure, hypertension, sodium restriction.
- Adjust in renal failure per label.

> Do not confuse trometamol (PO) with disodium (IV).

adulto.presentation: Trometamol sachet 3 g; IV disodium vial 1–4 g.
adulto.dose: Uncomplicated cystitis: **3 g PO (trometamol) once**. IV disodium: usual **4 g every 6–8 h** (frequent range **12–16 g/day**; special cases up to ~**24 g/day** under ID).
adulto.administration: PO: dissolve sachet in water, preferably fasting or away from meals. IV: reconstitute with sterile water; dilute (e.g. toward 4–40 mg/mL in 5% dextrose) and infuse ~1 g/h (no bolus).
adulto.notes: IV reconstitution: mild exothermic reaction expected.

pediatrico.presentation: IV vial 1 g; trometamol PO by age/weight and authorized product.
pediatrico.dose: IV: **200–400 mg/kg/day every 6–8 h**. PO trometamol in children: only if the product/label allows (many 3 g labels are adult); follow weight-based local pediatric label.
pediatrico.administration: Diluted slow IV. PO per sachet instructions.
pediatrico.notes: Calculate sodium load on high IV regimens.

neonatal.dose: ID/NNU only; dose and interval by gestational age — not the adult oral cystitis regimen.
neonatal.notes: Sodium content clinically relevant in preterms.

stability:
## Stability

- IV dilution: ~24 h at room temperature (check label).
- PO sachet: use immediately after dissolving.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Diarrhea, nausea, headache, pharyngitis/rhinitis. Serious (rare): aplastic anemia, cholestasis, hepatic necrosis, angioedema, toxic megacolon.
